title: Alan White (Oasis drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: Alan Victor 'Whitey' White, born 26 May 1972, Lewisham, London. Starclub 1991-1994, Dr Robert of the Blow Monkeys; joined Oasis in April 1995 after Tony McCarroll was removed, recommended to Noel Gallagher by Paul Weller; his first appearance a Top of the Pops playback of Some Might Say. Four studio albums (Morning Glory, Be Here Now, Standing on the Shoulder of Giants, Heathen Chemistry), most B-sides; left early 2004, replaced by Zak Starkey. Noel: he would adapt a song's rhythm or advise on tempo. Owen Morris: 'essentially a jazz drummer' who 'was always shuffling away on his snare ... and never hitting the basic back beats in a big dumb rock and roll way'. Brother Steve White (Paul Weller, the Style Council) 'greatly impacted his development'; other influences Keith Moon, Ringo Starr, Chad Smith, Mick Avory, John Bonham. Named for the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Oasis, 2026.

title: Alan White of Oasis (T. Bruce Wittet, Modern Drummer, August 1996; fan-site copy)
notes: Taught the Moeller system by Bob Armstrong: 'You move your arm up and drop the stick for a bounce and come down for a power-stroke'; 'the reason there are so many grace notes and bits and bobs in my drumming is that the way I play was the way I was taught by Bob Armstrong'. Influences: soul first, 'Clyde Stubblefield and all those guys' for the grooves and fills; then the Beatles, Kinks and Small Faces; Ringo ('It had to be Ringo'); Ginger Baker. Kit: an old Rogers Holiday kit with its original heads; his brother Steve's old Radio King snares (Champagne Supernova on a Radio King); big cymbals 'otherwise it just doesn't cut through'; Pearl and Sabian endorsements. Wonderwall: he came in on Noel's cue, not the top of the phrase, 'a bit of a weird one, but it worked!'. Don't Look Back in Anger: 'I can be straight ... because that's what's needed.' Champagne Supernova: 'I wish I had been a little heavier.' A fan site's copy of the magazine text.

title: Alan White - drummerszone.com profile
notes: Biography: Whirlpool with Gem Archer in 1987; Noel Gallagher said his style drew on funk drummers like Chad Smith; Sabian among his brands. Its header gives 1952 for his birth, its text 1972.

title: The Rise and Fall of Me Recording Oasis (Owen Morris)
notes: The producer's account, cited by Wikipedia: White 'essentially a jazz drummer', 'always shuffling away on his snare'; McCarroll's timing 'almost autistically perfect'. Read through Wikipedia's quotation; the archived page itself was not opened.

title: (What's the Story) Morning Glory? - Wikipedia
notes: Released 2 October 1995 (Creation), produced by Owen Morris and Noel Gallagher at Rockfield, May-June 1995. Personnel: Alan White drums and percussion on all but track 7 (Some Might Say), Tony McCarroll drums on 7. White's first live shows with the band the Bath Pavilion warm-up and Glastonbury, June 1995.

title: Be Here Now (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 21 August 1997 (Creation); the first album entirely with White on drums. D'You Know What I Mean? carries a slowed loop of N.W.A's Straight Outta Compton (the Amen break). Morris had wanted to overdub drums onto the Mustique demos.

title: Heathen Chemistry - Wikipedia
notes: 2002 (Big Brother); White's last Oasis album; drums on its tracks including The Hindu Times.

title: Wonderwall - Wikipedia
notes: Alan White drums; instead of sticks he used Pro-Mark Hot Rods, 'which provide a softer and more diffuse sound'. Rick Beato on the choice between sticks and brushes.

title: D'You Know What I Mean? - Wikipedia
notes: Single, July 1997; Noel: 'It's eight and a half minutes, the first single, the drums haven't fuckin' come in for two minutes'. Alan White drums.

title: Tony McCarroll - Wikipedia
notes: Oasis's drummer 1991-1995, on Definitely Maybe, Whatever and Some Might Say; dismissed April 1995 and replaced by Alan White. Noel: 'he wouldn't have been able to drum the new songs.'
